scope: Shared PET-GF profile audit and native bridge-flow translation; no production-profile change or new print

evidence.bridge_flow: v5 optical gap preference and v7 completed-roof preference favor 125% extrusion at fixed pitch and 70% fan; v7 R125 uses 25 mm/s.
evidence.bridge_speed: Mark2 F07 (15 mm/s) is reported less bad than F08 (25 mm/s) at 125% flow and 100% fan. This favors 15 within the local lateral-tooth geometry, without establishing a universal optimum. C03 at 15 is a possible pass; C04 at 25 is a candidate pass. The user specifically identifies 15 mm/s as a candidate for promotion.
evidence.ramps: All 16 v6 ramps at 35-42.5 degrees from the bed, both directions and 70/100% fan, are acceptable over 14 mm reach and 12 mm width. 100% has a modest reported finish benefit. This does not select 100% for bridges or establish larger-area performance.

native_check.conclusion: Normal native bridge flow 1.25 preserves the tested main-stroke XYZ and pitch and matches its commanded extrusion within rounding. It also increases four R125 Overhang-wall segment volumes by 25%, unlike the bridge-fill-only test treatment. Other matched R125 feature extrusion is unchanged. No test postprocessor is needed to store native bridge flow, but the native perimeter treatment still needs a physical surface check.

promotion_candidate.ordinary_layer_time_cooling: Retain current 0-70% behavior and first-three-layer cooling suppression; verify actual native bridge/ramp fan commands in the candidate slice.
promotion_candidate.100_percent_ramp_cooling: Optional local treatment for ramp-dominated finish, not a shared bridge-fan selection.
promotion_candidate.support_threshold: No proposed global change; the saved setting is already 35.

remaining_work: Prepare a candidate from the shared profile and inspect its emitted E, pitch, speed, fan and bridge/perimeter ordering on a 12 mm bridge and 35/40 degree ramps.

Print a small check directly from that native candidate: exposed first bridge layer, completed roof, and ramps. Compare gap closure and retained shape with the preferred samples; inspect the native bridge-perimeter treatment. No additional broad flow sweep is required.

Save the selected process and first PET-GF filament values consistently in petgf.3mf, read them back from a fresh slice, and commit/push the profile and the physical result. Fin-release qualification is separate.
status: Native bridge-flow translation checked; shared production profile unchanged; candidate physical check and profile promotion remain outstanding.
